questions.question: Telangana's vision is to achieve a $3 trillion State GDP by __ __.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2047**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of Telangana** has formulated a strategic long-term vision to elevate the state's **Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP)** to **3 trillion dollars** by the year **2047**.
 
• This ambitious economic roadmap is integrated with the broader national objective of **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**, which aims to transform India into a developed nation by the **centenary of its independence**.
 
• The vision emphasizes a multi-sectoral growth strategy, focusing on high-value industries such as **Information Technology (IT)**, **Biotechnology**, **Aerospace**, and **Precision Engineering** to drive the economy forward.
 
• To achieve this **3 trillion dollar** milestone, the state plans to leverage its capital, **Hyderabad**, as a global hub for the **Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)** and **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**.
 
• The roadmap includes significant investments in infrastructure, such as the **Regional Ring Road (RRR)** and the development of **Future Cities**, to facilitate seamless trade and industrial expansion.
 
• Strategic policy interventions are designed to maintain a consistent **Double-Digit Growth Rate** over the coming decades, ensuring that Telangana remains a primary engine of India's economic growth.
 
• Therefore, the year **2047** is the target year for achieving this specific economic scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viksit Telangana Framework**:

 
 
• **Economic Diversification**: The state is moving beyond traditional services into **Semiconductor Manufacturing** and **Green Energy** to ensure a resilient 3 trillion dollar economy.
 
• **Per Capita Income**: Telangana currently boasts one of the highest **Per Capita Incomes** in India, which serves as a foundational strength for the **2047** vision.
 
• **Urbanization and Growth**: The state government is focusing on creating **Industrial Clusters** in tier-2 and tier-3 cities like **Warangal**, **Khammam**, and **Karimnagar** to decentralize growth.
 
• **Life Sciences Ecosystem**: Telangana aims to capture a significant share of the global pharmaceutical market, targeting a sectoral valuation of **250 billion dollars** by **2030** as a stepping stone toward the final **2047** goal.

questions.question: All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey (NAFIS) is conducted by which organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey (NAFIS)** is a comprehensive national-level primary survey conducted by the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**.
 
• The survey aims to provide a holistic assessment of the **rural financial landscape** by collecting data on **livelihoods**, **income**, **expenditure**, **savings**, **debts**, and **insurance** patterns of households.
 
• The first edition, **NAFIS 2016-17**, was released in **August 2018**, covering approximately 40,327 households across the country to establish a benchmark for **financial inclusion**.
 
• The second edition, **NAFIS 2021-22**, was released in **August 2024**, providing updated insights into the financial health of **rural** and **semi-urban** populations in the post-pandemic era.
 
• The survey is unique as it captures data on both **agricultural** and **non-agricultural** households, measuring the depth of **institutional credit** penetration in remote areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD**:

 
 
• It was established on **July 12, 1982**, based on the recommendations of the **B. Sivaraman Committee** through the **NABARD Act 1981**.
 
• It serves as the apex regulatory body for the **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)** and **Apex Cooperative Banks** in India.
 
• The institution is headquartered in **Mumbai** and operates under the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• While the **RBI** constructs the annual **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** to monitor inclusion levels, the specific **NAFIS** field survey is exclusively a **NABARD** initiative.
 
 
 
• **CII and FICCI**:
 
 
• The **Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)** and the **Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI)** are non-governmental **industry associations**.
 
• They focus on **policy advocacy** and business networking rather than conducting official government-backed rural financial surveys.

questions.question: Which software helps in maintaining and optimizing the system e.g., disk cleanup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Utility software**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Utility software** is a type of **system software** specifically designed to help analyze, configure, **optimize**, or maintain a computer.
 
• Unlike application software, which focuses on user-centric tasks, utility software focuses on the **internal infrastructure** and **hardware management** of the computer system.
 
• **Disk Cleanup** is a prominent example of a utility program that identifies and removes unnecessary files, such as **temporary internet files** and **system logs**, to enhance system performance and reclaim storage space.
 
• These programs provide **preventative maintenance** and **system protection**, ensuring that the operating system runs smoothly and securely.
 
• Other critical examples of utility software include **disk defragmenters**, **antivirus programs**, **file compression tools** (like WinZip), and **backup utilities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Programming software**:

 
 
• Refers to tools and programs that assist developers in creating, debugging, and maintaining other software applications.
 
• Key components include **Compilers**, **Interpreters**, **Debuggers**, and **Integrated Development Environments (IDEs)** like Visual Studio or Eclipse.
 
 
 
• **Firmware**:
 
 
• A specific class of computer software that provides low-level control for a device's specific hardware.
 
• It is usually stored in **Read-Only Memory (ROM)** or **Flash memory** and includes the **BIOS/UEFI** found on computer motherboards.
 
 
 
• **Application software**:
 
 
• Software designed to perform a specific group of coordinated functions or tasks for the benefit of the user.
 
• Common examples include **word processors** (MS Word), **spreadsheets** (MS Excel), **web browsers**, and **database management systems**.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India introduced Fundamental Duties in the form of Article 51A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42ⁿd Amendment, 1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in **1976** during the **Internal Emergency** (1975−1977), is the most comprehensive amendment in Indian history, often referred to as the **Mini-Constitution**.
 
• This amendment inserted **Part IV-A** and **Article 51A** into the Constitution, which originally enumerated **ten Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was incorporated based on the recommendations of the **Sardar Swaran Singh Committee**, which was constituted by the government in **1976** to suggest changes to the Constitution.
 
• These duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former **USSR** (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) and serve as a reminder to citizens that while they enjoy rights, they also have duties toward the nation.
 
• In addition to Fundamental Duties, this amendment also added the words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** to the **Preamble** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **24th Amendment, 1971**

 
 
• This amendment was enacted to neutralize the effects of the **Golaknath case** judgement.
 
• It affirmed the power of the **Parliament** to amend any part of the Constitution, including **Fundamental Rights**, and made it obligatory for the **President** to give assent to Constitutional Amendment Bills.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment, 1978**
 
 
• Introduced by the **Janata Party** government to reverse several changes made by the **42ⁿd Amendment** and provide safeguards against future misuse of emergency powers.
 
• It notably deleted the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **52ⁿd Amendment, 1985**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it added the **Tenth Schedule** to the Constitution.
 
• It provides for the disqualification of members of **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** on the grounds of defection from one political party to another.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes ‘disguised unemployment’ in the Indian context?

options.text: Workers are temporarily unemployed during economic slowdown.
Workers are not willing to work.
More people are employed than actually needed, with marginal productivity being zero.
Workers shift from one job to another frequently.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More people are employed than actually needed, with marginal productivity being zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised unemployment** is a phenomenon where the number of people working on a specific task is significantly higher than the number actually required to complete it.
 
• The defining characteristic of this state is that the **Marginal Productivity** of the extra labor is **zero**, meaning that if these surplus workers are removed, the **total production** or output will not decrease.
 
• In the **Indian context**, this is most prevalent in the **Agricultural sector**, where large families often work on small land holdings because of a lack of alternative employment opportunities in **manufacturing** or **services**.
 
• It is also referred to as **hidden unemployment** because the individuals appear to be fully employed, but their labor contribution is technically redundant to the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Unemployment:
 
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**: Occurs when there is a lack of aggregate demand in the economy, typically during an **economic slowdown** or **recession**.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment**: A temporary period of unemployment that occurs when a worker is **shifting from one job to another** or searching for a new position.
 
• **Structural Unemployment**: Results from a mismatch between the **skills** possessed by the workforce and the skills required by employers, often driven by **technological advancement**.
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**: Occurs when people are unemployed at certain times of the year when demand for labor is low, such as in **agriculture** after the harvesting season or in the **tourism industry**.
 
• **Vulnerable Employment**: Refers to people working informally without proper **job contracts** or **social security** benefits, which is a major challenge in the **Indian labor market**.

questions.question: Which part of Windows 10 OS settings can you use to change when the computer enters Power Saving Mode?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power & Sleep Settings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Windows 10**, the **Power & Sleep Settings** menu is the primary interface used to manage how the computer consumes energy during periods of inactivity.
 
• This section allows users to specify separate time intervals for the **Screen** to turn off and for the PC to enter **Sleep Mode** (a low-power state that saves open apps to memory).
 
• The configuration provides granular control by allowing different timers for when the device is **On battery power** versus when it is **Plugged in** to an external power source.
 
• Setting shorter durations for entering **Power Saving Mode** is a critical step for preserving **Battery life** on portable devices like laptops and tablets.
 
• To navigate to this section, users must click the **Start** button, select the **Settings** gear icon, choose **System**, and then click on **Power & sleep** in the left-hand sidebar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Network & Internet**:

 
 
• Manages all connectivity features including **Wi-Fi**, **Ethernet**, **VPN**, **Dial-up**, and **Proxy** settings.
 
• Includes tools like **Network Reset** and monitoring of **Data usage**.
 
 
 
• **Display Settings**:
 
 
• Controls visual output parameters such as **Brightness**, **Resolution**, **Orientation**, and **Scaling**.
 
• Houses settings for **HDR** (High Dynamic Range) and **Night light** filters.
 
 
 
• **Updates & Security**:
 
 
• Responsible for **Windows Update**, **Windows Security**, **Recovery** options, and **Activation**.
 
• Used to schedule system restarts after updates have been downloaded.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word 2016 and later versions, when text spanning multiple paragraphs is highlighted and the user presses Ctrl + C, what operation is performed?

options.text: Immediately inserts the paragraphs at the document's beginning
Automatically saves the entire document with paragraphs updated
Permanently erases the highlighted paragraphs from existence
Transfers the highlighted paragraphs to clipboard for duplication elsewhere

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transfers the highlighted paragraphs to clipboard for duplication elsewhere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + C** is a standard keyboard shortcut used in **Microsoft Word 2016** and later versions to execute the **Copy** command, which duplicates selected content.
 
• When multiple paragraphs are highlighted, pressing this shortcut sends a copy of the **text**, **paragraph formatting**, and any associated **metadata** to the **Windows System Clipboard**.
 
• The **Clipboard** is a temporary storage buffer located in the computer's **Random Access Memory (RAM)** that holds data until it is overwritten or the system is shut down.
 
• Unlike the **Cut** command, **Copy** is a non-destructive operation, meaning the original paragraphs remain in their initial position within the document while a replica is made available for use.
 
• In **Office 365** and **Microsoft Word 2016/2019**, the **Office Clipboard** can store up to **24 items**, allowing users to collect multiple snippets of information and paste them selectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Related Shortcut Commands:
 
 
• **Ctrl + V (Paste)**: This command retrieves the most recent item from the **Clipboard** and inserts it at the current **Insertion Point** or replaces a selected block of text.
 
• **Ctrl + X (Cut)**: This function removes the highlighted paragraphs from the document and places them on the **Clipboard**, effectively facilitating a **Move** operation.
 
• **Ctrl + S (Save)**: This shortcut triggers the **Save** function, committing the current state of the document to the **Hard Drive** or **Cloud Storage** (like OneDrive) to prevent data loss.
 
• **Windows Key + V**: In modern **Windows 10** and **11** environments, this shortcut opens the **Clipboard History**, allowing users to access multiple previously copied paragraphs or images.

questions.question: A physics lab experiment requires the measurement of temperature using the correct SI unit. Which unit should the student use to record temperature readings according to the SI system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelvin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kelvin** (symbol: **K**) is the primary base unit of **thermodynamic temperature** in the **International System of Units (SI)**.
 
• Unlike the Celsius or Fahrenheit scales, the Kelvin scale is an **absolute scale**, meaning it begins at **absolute zero** (0 K), the point at which all thermal motion of particles ceases.
 
• Since 2019, the Kelvin has been defined by the fixed numerical value of the **Boltzmann constant (k)**, which is 1.380649 × 10−²³ when expressed in the unit **J K−¹**.
 
• In scientific research and **physics laboratory experiments**, Kelvin is the standard because it allows for direct proportionality in thermodynamic equations, such as the **Ideal Gas Law** (PV = nRT).
 
• The magnitude of one Kelvin is exactly equal to the magnitude of one **degree Celsius**; however, the two scales differ by an offset of **273.15** units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celsius**

 
 
• A derived **SI unit** commonly used for everyday temperature measurements.
 
• 0 °C is defined as **273.15 K**, which is approximately the freezing point of water.
 
 
 
• **Fahrenheit**
 
 
• A non-SI temperature scale used primarily in the **United States**.
 
• The conversion formula to Celsius is °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9.
 
 
 
• **Joule**
 
 
• The **SI unit of energy**, work, or heat.
 
• It is a derived unit defined as one **Newton-meter** (1 J = 1 kg m² s−²).

questions.question: Who was the great general responsible for executing Alauddin Khilji’s Deccan campaigns successfully?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malik Kafur**__.

__
 
• **Malik Kafur**, also known as **Hazardinari** (meaning bought for a thousand dinars), was a prominent slave-general of **Alauddin Khilji**, the Sultan of Delhi.
 
• He was captured by **Nusrat Khan** during the invasion of **Gujarat** in **1299 CE** and subsequently rose to the highest military rank of **Naib (Viceroy)** in the Sultanate.
 
• Between **1309 and 1311 CE**, Kafur led the **Deccan campaigns**, making the Delhi Sultanate the first northern Islamic power to reach the southern tip of the Indian peninsula.
 
• His successful military expeditions subdued several powerful southern dynasties, including the **Yadavas of Devagiri** (King Ramachandra), the **Kakatiyas of Warangal** (King Prataparudra II), the **Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra** (Vira Ballala III), and the **Pandyas of Madurai**.
 
• These campaigns were focused on establishing **suzerainty** and collecting vast spoils of war, including **gold, jewelry, horses, and elephants**, rather than direct administrative annexation of the southern territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**:

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Tughlaq Dynasty** (1320–1325 CE) and is known for building the fortified city of **Tughlaqabad**.
 
 
 
• **Balban**:
 
 
• A powerful ruler of the **Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty** (1266–1287 CE), famous for his policy of **Blood and Iron** and the introduction of **Sijda and Paibos**.
 
 
 
• **Qutbuddin Aibak**:
 
 
• The first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate and founder of the **Slave Dynasty** (1206–1210 CE), who began the construction of the **Qutub Minar**.

__
 
• The **30 kW IDD&IS Mk-IIA**, also known by its nickname **Sahastra Shakti**, is an advanced **Directed Energy Weapon (DEW)** successfully field-tested by the **DRDO** on **April 13, 2025**.

• Technically, the **Mk-IIA** variant utilizes a **30-kilowatt** laser output generated by combining six individual **5 kW fiber laser sources** in a **2×3 configuration** to achieve a precision 'hard kill'.
 
• The system is integrated with **radar** and **Electro-Optical/Infrared (EO/IR)** sensors for automated target detection and tracking, allowing it to destroy enemy sensors or airframes within seconds.
 
• Following its successful evaluation, **DRDO** initiated the **Transfer of Technology (ToT)** to private sector partners to begin **serial production**, supporting the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in defense manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs)**:

 
 
• These systems offer a revolutionary **low cost-per-shot**, with each engagement costing approximately the same as a few liters of fuel, compared to expensive traditional interceptor missiles.
 
• India is now part of an exclusive group of nations, including the **USA, Russia, and China**, that possess operational high-power laser weapon capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of IDD&IS**:
 
 
• The **Mk-I** version featured a **2 kW** laser used primarily for soft-kill or short-range operations, while the **Mk-II** was a **10 kW** system.
 
• The **30 kW Mk-IIA** represents a significant scale-up in power, allowing for the neutralization of larger aerial threats and coordinated **swarm attacks**.

questions.question: Which Charter Act ended the East India Company’s monopoly over trade with India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1813**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** was passed by the **British Parliament** to renew the charter of the **East India Company** for another 20 years.
 
• The most significant feature of this Act was the **abolition of the commercial monopoly** of the East India Company in India, effectively opening **Indian trade** to all **British merchants**.
 
• The Act asserted the **sovereignty of the British Crown** over the Indian territories held by the Company, marking a shift toward formal imperial control.
 
• While it ended the general trade monopoly, the Company was still allowed to retain its monopoly over the **trade in tea** and the **trade with China**.
 
• The Act mandated a sum of **one lakh rupees** to be set aside annually for the **revival of literature** and the promotion of **modern sciences** among the inhabitants of the British territories in India.
 
• It granted formal permission to **Christian missionaries** to enter India for the purpose of **religious proselytization** and promoting moral improvements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1833**:

 
 
• It completely ended the Company's monopoly, including the **tea trade** and **trade with China**, making it a purely administrative body.
 
• The **Governor-General of Bengal** was designated as the **Governor-General of India**, with **Lord William Bentinck** being the first to hold this title.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1853**:
 
 
• It introduced an **open competition system** for the recruitment of **civil servants**, ending the patronage system.
 
• It separated the **legislative** and **executive functions** of the Governor-General’s Council for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1793**:
 
 
• This Act renewed the Company's commercial privileges for 20 years and mandated that the **salaries of the Board of Control** members be paid out of **Indian revenues**.

questions.question: Which of the following substances should be added to acidic soil to neutralize it effectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quicklime (calcium oxide)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil acidity** is characterized by a low pH value (below 7.0), resulting from an excess of **hydrogen ions (H+)** and a deficiency of basic cations like **calcium** and **magnesium**.
 
• **Quicklime**, scientifically known as **calcium oxide (CaO)**, is an **alkaline substance** frequently used in agriculture to raise the pH level of acidic soils to a range suitable for crop production, typically between 6.0 and 7.0.
 
• When **Quicklime** is applied to the soil, it reacts with water in a process called **slaking** (CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂), forming **calcium hydroxide**, which releases **hydroxide ions (OH−)** that neutralize the acidic **hydrogen ions**.
 
• This chemical **neutralization** helps prevent **aluminum and manganese toxicity**, which occurs at low pH levels and can severely stunt root development and overall plant growth.
 
• The use of **Quicklime** is considered more effective for rapid correction of soil acidity compared to **agricultural limestone (calcium carbonate)** due to its higher solubility and faster reaction rate in the soil profile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking soda (Sodium bicarbonate)**:

 
 
• While **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)** is basic, its use in soil is limited because it adds **sodium**, which causes **soil sodicity**, degrades soil structure, and can be toxic to most agricultural plants.
 
 
 
• **Table salt (Sodium chloride)**:
 
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** is a neutral salt and does not possess any properties to neutralize acidity. High concentrations of salt lead to **soil salinization**, causing **osmotic stress** that prevents plants from absorbing water.
 
 
 
• **Vinegar**:
 
 
• Vinegar is a dilute solution of **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)**. Adding an acid to already acidic soil would further lower the pH, increasing acidity and potentially damaging **beneficial soil microorganisms** and plant tissues.

questions.question: What was proven to exist in an atom, by Rutherford's gold foil experiment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1911**, **Ernest Rutherford** conducted the **Alpha-ray scattering experiment** by bombarding a very thin **gold foil** with high-energy **alpha particles** (doubly charged helium ions).
 
• The experiment revealed that while most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection, a small fraction was diverted at large angles, and approximately 1 in 12,000 particles bounced back nearly **180 degrees**.
 
• Rutherford concluded that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** of an atom are not uniformly distributed but are concentrated in an extremely small, dense region at the center.
 
• This central core was named the **nucleus**, proving that atoms consist of a tiny, massive, and positively charged center surrounded by mostly **empty space**.
 
• This discovery successfully refuted the **Thomson Plum Pudding Model**, which suggested that positive charge was spread evenly throughout the atom like a pudding.

• Discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** using the **Cathode Ray Tube** experiment.
 
• These are negatively charged subatomic particles that reside in the space surrounding the **nucleus** in specific **energy levels** or orbits.
 
 
 
• **Proton**:
 
 
• While the concept of a positive charge was established by Rutherford in 1911, he specifically identified the **hydrogen nucleus** as a fundamental particle called the **proton** in **1919** through nitrogen bombardment experiments.
 
• Protons carry a positive charge equal in magnitude to the negative charge of an electron.
 
 
 
• **Neutron**:
 
 
• Discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**.
 
• These are electrically **neutral** particles located inside the **nucleus** alongside protons, accounting for the remaining mass of the atom that protons alone could not explain.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford Atomic Model**:
 
 
• Proposed that **electrons** revolve around the **nucleus** in circular paths called **orbits**, similar to how planets revolve around the sun in the solar system.

questions.question: Which of the following devices can act as both an input as well as an output device?
questions.solution:

__
 
• A **Touchscreen** is a unique peripheral that combines the capabilities of an **input device** and an **output device** within a single physical unit.
 
• It functions as an **input device** by utilizing a touch-sensitive overlay that detects the pressure or electrical conductivity of a finger or **stylus**, converting these physical interactions into digital signals for the processor.
 
• Simultaneously, it serves as an **output device** by using an integrated **LCD (Liquid Crystal Display)** or **OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode)** panel to display visual information and feedback to the user.
 
• Common technologies used in these devices include **Capacitive** sensing (relying on electrical charges) and **Resistive** sensing (relying on physical pressure), both of which allow for direct interaction with a **Graphical User Interface (GUI)**.
 
• Because it both receives data from the user and provides data back to the user on the same interface, it is classified as a **dual-purpose** or **hybrid peripheral**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• This is a dedicated **input device** that uses a **laser beam** or an **image sensor** to scan and decode the printed bars of a barcode.
 
• It transmits the decoded numerical or alphanumeric data into a computer system for processing, but it cannot display information to the user.
 
 
 
• **Plotter**:
 
 
• A **Plotter** is a specialized **output device** used for printing **vector graphics**.
 
• Unlike standard printers, it uses **automated pens** to draw continuous, high-precision lines on large sheets of paper, making it essential for **Computer-Aided Design (CAD)**, engineering blueprints, and architectural plans.
 
 
 
• **Digital Camera**:
 
 
• In a computing context, a digital camera is primarily viewed as an **input device** because it captures light through a lens and converts it into digital data via **CCD (Charge-Coupled Device)** or **CMOS sensors**.
 
• This data is then transferred into a computer or storage medium for later viewing or editing.

• The **Montreal Protocol** on Substances that Deplete the **Ozone Layer** is a global agreement finalized in **1987** and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**.

• The treaty targets several groups of halogenated hydrocarbons, including **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **Halons**, **Carbon tetrachloride**, and **Methyl chloroform**.
 
• It is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties, being the first to achieve **universal ratification** by all **198 UN Member States**.
 
• To commemorate its signing, **September 16** is observed annually as **World Ozone Day**.
 
• The **Kigali Amendment (2016)** is a recent addition to the protocol aimed at phasing down **Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)**, which are potent greenhouse gases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It promotes the **wise use** of wetlands and identifies sites of international importance to maintain ecological health.

questions.question: India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) to boost global trade participation. In which year did India join the WTO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India is a **founding member** of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, having joined the organization on the very day of its inception, **January 1, 1995**.
 
• The WTO was established as the successor to the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**, which had been in place since **1948**; India was also a founding member of GATT.
 
• The transition from GATT to the WTO was formalized through the **Marrakesh Agreement**, signed in **April 1994** in Morocco, following the conclusion of the **Uruguay Round** of trade negotiations.
 
• By becoming a member, India committed to a rule-based **multilateral trading system** designed to ensure transparency, predictability, and the reduction of trade barriers like **tariffs** and **quotas**.
 
• Membership allows India to invoke the **Dispute Settlement Mechanism** of the WTO to protect its commercial interests against unfair trade practices by other nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:

 
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, and serves as the primary forum for negotiating global trade rules.
 
• Its core principles include **Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN)** treatment (treating all members equally) and **National Treatment** (treating foreigners and locals equally).
 
• The WTO covers trade in **goods**, **services** (GATS), and **intellectual property** (TRIPS), which was a significant expansion over the original GATT framework.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• **1991**: Although India did not join the WTO this year, it was a pivotal year for the Indian economy as it launched **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms under the leadership of **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
 
• **2001**: This year saw the initiation of the **Doha Development Round** at the fourth WTO Ministerial Conference, which focused on improving the trading prospects of **developing nations**.
 
• **Uruguay Round**: Conducted from **1986 to 1994**, this was the 8th round of multilateral trade negotiations and the largest ever, directly leading to the creation of the WTO.

questions.question: The Harappan Civilization flourished mainly during which of the following archaeological eras?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronze Age**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, is classified as a **Bronze Age** culture because its inhabitants mastered the art of metallurgy, specifically the production of **bronze**.
 
• Technologically, the Harappans created **bronze** by alloying **copper**, which they primarily sourced from the **Khetri mines** in **Rajasthan**, with **tin**, which was largely imported from regions like **Afghanistan** and **Hazaribagh**.
 
• Archaeological evidence from major urban centers such as **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa** reveals advanced bronze artifacts, including the famous **Dancing Girl** figurine, manufactured using the sophisticated **lost-wax casting** (cire perdue) technique.
 
• The civilization reached its **Mature Phase** between approximately **2600 BCE and 1900 BCE**, characterized by planned cities, drainage systems, and the widespread use of bronze for crafting tools, weapons, and ornaments.
 
• While the civilization used stone tools, the dominance of bronze for specialized craftsmanship and trade distinguishes it from the preceding stone-based eras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neolithic Age**

 
 
• This era represents the **New Stone Age**, marked by the transition from hunting-gathering to **agriculture** and **animal husbandry**.
 
• The site of **Mehrgarh** in present-day **Pakistan** is a significant precursor, showing early farming practices that eventually evolved into the urban Harappan stage.
 
 
 
• **Chalcolithic Age**
 
 
• Known as the **Copper-Stone Age**, this period involved the use of both **stone tools** and **copper**.
 
• Various regional cultures like the **Ahar-Banas** and **Kayatha** flourished in India, often overlapping with or succeeding the Harappan timeline in different geographies.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age**
 
 
• The **Iron Age** in the Indian subcontinent began long after the decline of the Harappan Civilization, starting roughly around **1000 BCE**.
 
• The **Indus people** had no knowledge of **iron**; the metal only became prominent during the **Later Vedic Period** and the era of the **Mahajanapadas**.

• Cotton is an **agro-based** raw material that undergoes a series of transformations including **ginning** (separation of fiber from seeds), **spinning** (converting fiber into yarn), and **weaving** or **knitting** (converting yarn into fabric).
 
• In the Indian context, the **Cotton Textile Industry** is highly significant, providing massive **employment** and contributing nearly 2 percent to the **total GDP** of the country.
 
• The industry is geographically concentrated in states like **Maharashtra** and **Gujarat** due to the availability of **raw cotton**, proximity to markets, and favorable **moist climatic conditions** for spinning.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is the Dilwara Temple, which exhibits a distinct architectural style that fuses elements of Jain, Hindu, and even Mughal craftsmanship, located?

__
 
• The **Dilwara Temples** are a group of five world-renowned marble Jain temples located about 2.5 kilometers from **Mount Abu**, the only hill station in **Rajasthan**.
 
• These temples were built between the **11th and 16th centuries AD** and are considered masterpieces of **Maru-Gurjara architecture**, characterized by incredible intricate carvings on white marble.
 
• The complex is situated in the **Sirohi district** amidst the lush green hills of the **Aravalli Range**, which is the oldest fold mountain range in India.
 
• The most famous among them, the **Vimal Vasahi Temple**, was constructed in **1031 AD** by **Vimal Shah**, a minister of the Solanki ruler of Gujarat, and is dedicated to the first Tirthankara, **Lord Rishabhdeva**.
 
• Another significant shrine is the **Luna Vasahi Temple**, built in **1230 AD** by the brothers **Vastupala and Tejpal**, which is dedicated to the 22nd Tirthankara, **Lord Neminatha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Elements**:

 
 
• The temples are famous for their **ornamental vaulted ceilings**, **pillars**, and **toranas** (arched gateways) that display minute details of dancers, musicians, and floral patterns.
 
• While primarily Jain in nature, the evolution of the site over centuries saw the integration of regional **Hindu** motifs and, in later structures, subtle refinements in stonework often associated with the high precision of later **Indian craftsmanship**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Although the patrons (Solankis) were from the **Gujarat region**, the physical site of **Mount Abu** falls within the administrative boundaries of **Rajasthan**.
 
• Gujarat is home to other major Jain sites like **Palitana** and **Girnar**, which share similar architectural DNA.
 
 
 
• **Key Shrines**:
 
 
• The five temples are **Vimal Vasahi**, **Luna Vasahi**, **Pitalhar**, **Parshvanatha**, and **Mahavir Swami**, each dedicated to different **Jain Tirthankaras**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the constitution of Gram Sabha?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Article 243A** of the Indian Constitution specifies the establishment, powers, and functions of the **Gram Sabha** at the village level.
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** added **Part IX** to the Constitution, which established a three-tier **Panchayati Raj System** in India to facilitate rural local governance.
 
• A **Gram Sabha** is defined under **Article 243(b)** as a local body consisting of all individuals registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area.
 
• Under **Article 243A**, the Gram Sabha is empowered to exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the **Legislature of a State** may provide by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 243B (Constitution of Panchayats):**

 
 
• This article mandates the establishment of a three-tier local governance structure in every state: the **village level**, the **intermediate level**, and the **district level**.
 
• States with a population not exceeding **twenty lakhs** (2 million) are exempt from constituting Panchayats at the intermediate level.
 
 
 
• **Article 224A (Appointment of Retired Judges):**
 
 
• This article permits the **Chief Justice of a High Court**, with the prior consent of the **President of India**, to request a retired High Court judge to sit and act as a judge of that High Court.
 
 
 
• **Article 224 (Appointment of Additional and Acting Judges):**
 
 
• While **Article 224B** is not a valid provision, **Article 224** deals with the appointment of temporary additional and acting judges to clear pending cases or address temporary increases in High Court workloads.

questions.question: The Terai belt is best described as:

options.text: A dry zone made of calcareous deposits

A marshy tract with a high water table and thick forests

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A marshy tract with a high water table and thick forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Terai** is a lowland belt located south of the **outer foothills** of the **Himalayas** and the **Bhabar** region, spanning across parts of **India** and **Nepal**.
 
• It is characterized by a **high water table** because the streams and rivers that disappear into the **porous** rocks of the **Bhabar** zone re-emerge at the surface in this region.
 
• The re-emergence of these underground water sources creates a **damp**, **swampy**, and **marshy tract** that is naturally conducive to the growth of **thick forests** and tall grasslands.
 
• This region is historically known for its **immense biodiversity** and rich wildlife; however, over the years, significant portions have been cleared for **agriculture** to support settlement and crop production like **sugarcane**, **rice**, and **wheat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Northern Plains** of India are divided into four distinct physiological regions based on relief features:

 
 
• **Bhabar**: A narrow belt of about **8 to 16 km** in width lying parallel to the **Shiwalik** slopes, consisting of **pebbles** where rivers disappear.
 
• **Bhangar**: The largest part of the northern plain formed of **older alluvium**; it lies above the floodplains and contains **calcareous deposits** known as **Kankar**.
 
• **Khadar**: The **newer, younger alluvium** of the floodplains which is renewed almost every year, making the land highly **fertile** and ideal for **intensive agriculture**.
